issue.title: Follow-up to #745/#755: recompiled bundle shows prompt-insensitive output
issue.body:
# Context

Direct follow-up to #745/#755. #755 fixed a corpus record-ordering bug that was corrupting per-story context reconstruction at compile time, and ran a decisive before/after test: recompiling `smollm2-135m-instruct` from its existing, unmodified corpus bytes (fix applied, nothing else changed) turned a ~199s hang followed by single-token-cycling garbage into a ~0.2s answer in real, grammatical English. That result substantially answered #745's central question (word salad was largely an aggregation bug, not an architectural ceiling), and #745 was closed on that basis.

But the post-fix output had a second, separate problem that #755 explicitly did not investigate: **the bundle returned the same generated text for different prompts.** This issue exists to give that observation its own scope, since it's a distinct question from "does the architecture produce coherent English at all" (settled positive by #755) — this is "does the architecture actually condition its output on the prompt."

# The observation

Using the `smollm2-135m-instruct-755fix` bundle from #755's decisive test (recompiled via `r4 transformerless compile-recorded` from `smollm2-135m-instruct`'s real corpus, fix applied, teacher not re-run):

- `r4 ask --model smollm2-135m-instruct-755fix "What is April?"` → grammatical English about cities, populations, and Earth's atmosphere (topically unrelated to the prompt, but that alone isn't this issue's concern — see #745's own history on topic quality).
- `r4 ask --model smollm2-135m-instruct-755fix "Tell me about art."` → **the same output**, or output indistinguishable from the first, modulo the specific text not being independently recorded token-for-token in #755's writeup.
- `r4 ask --model smollm2-135m-instruct-755fix "Explain how computers work."` → again, the same/indistinguishable output.

This was noted qualitatively in #755's write-up on #745 but not measured rigorously — no controlled comparison across a larger prompt set, no token-level diff between runs, no check of whether the *first few* tokens (which would be most directly prompt-conditioned, before the compiler's own context window takes over) differ at all between prompts.

# Why this matters

If output is genuinely prompt-invariant, the compiled bundle is not actually functioning as a conditional language model in any usable sense — it's closer to sampling from an unconditional corpus-level distribution, regardless of what's asked. That would cap real-world usefulness even though #755 demonstrated the underlying text can be grammatical. This is a materially different failure mode from #745's (garbage syntax) and deserves its own root-cause investigation rather than being folded into #745 after the fact or left as an unverified aside.

It's also not yet established whether this is: (a) a genuine architectural/serving limitation (e.g. the prompt isn't actually seeding the generation context, or the teacher-forced witness lookup falls back to an unconditional path), (b) a capacity/corpus-scale artifact specific to this smaller bundle (`smollm2-135m-instruct` is the smallest locally compiled bundle; a larger corpus or context window might resolve it), or (c) a measurement artifact of only having tried three prompts informally.

# Scope

- Build a controlled, reproducible comparison: run `r4 ask` against the `smollm2-135m-instruct` (post-#755-fix) bundle with a meaningfully sized, varied prompt set (at least ~10-20 prompts spanning different topics/lengths/structures), record full output for each, and quantify overlap (exact match, shared n-gram prefix length, edit distance, or similar) rather than relying on spot-checking.
- Trace how the prompt actually enters generation: find where `r4 ask`/the transformerless serving path seeds initial context from the user's prompt (tokenizes it, looks up witnesses for its trailing tokens, etc.) and confirm empirically whether different prompts actually produce different initial lookups/witnesses, or whether they collapse to the same context key early (which would explain identical output directly, and would parallel #755's own BOS-collapse mechanism in spirit).
- Determine whether this is scale-sensitive: if feasible, run the same comparison against a larger already-compiled bundle (e.g. `smollm2-360m-broad` if its corpus can be run through `compile-recorded`, or any other available bundle above `smollm2-135m-instruct`'s size) and check whether prompt-sensitivity improves, stays flat, or is bundle-independent.
- Write up findings (positive or negative) in `docs/RESEARCH.md`'s research log per this repo's standard evidenced-research discipline, and post a summary back to whichever issue tracks the parent decision point (this issue itself, cross-referenced from #745).

# Non-goals

- Not re-litigating #745/#755's own conclusion (record-ordering bug was a major contributor to word-salad output) — that finding stands regardless of this issue's outcome.
- Not attempting to fix the topic-wandering/coherence-length problem noted in #755's write-up unless it turns out to share a root cause with prompt-insensitivity — those may be entangled but are conceptually separate (a model can wander between unrelated topics while still visibly responding differently to different prompts, and vice versa).
- Not assuming the answer is a bug at all — a corpus-scale/capacity explanation (b above) would be a legitimate, documentable negative-or-conditional finding, not a failure to close this issue.

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A controlled multi-prompt comparison (not ad hoc spot-checks) is run against the post-#755-fix `smollm2-135m-instruct` bundle and its degree of prompt-sensitivity is quantified.
- [ ] The mechanism by which the prompt seeds generation context is traced and directly implicated or ruled out as the cause of any observed insensitivity.
- [ ] If a scale comparison is feasible within reasonable effort, it's attempted and the result (improves / flat / inconclusive) is recorded honestly either way.
- [ ] Findings are recorded in `docs/RESEARCH.md` regardless of outcome (including a negative or inconclusive result), consistent with this repo's pre-declared-exit-rule / recorded-negative-result discipline.

# Verification

Full ladder if any code changes result: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --offline -- -D warnings`, `cargo run -p xtask -- audit-limits`, `cargo test --workspace --offline`. If this issue's work is purely measurement/tracing with no code change, the multi-prompt comparison data and the prompt-seeding trace are the verification artifacts themselves and should be reproducible from the write-up.

References #745, #755

comments.body:
Starting on this one, continuing directly from tonight's #755 work.

Working in `.worktrees/i758-prompt-insensitivity` off `main@05f4067c` (post-#755 merge).

Plan, following this issue's own proposed shape: first rebuild the `smollm2-135m-instruct` bundle from its existing corpus via `r4 transformerless compile-recorded` (same approach as #755's decisive test, now with the fix already in `main`) so there's a clean, reproducible artifact to test against — the one used in #755's write-up was an ad hoc local build outside git and has since been cleaned up. Then build a controlled multi-prompt comparison (real prompt set, not spot-checks) and quantify overlap before touching any serving code, so the write-up rests on measurement rather than the three-prompt impression from #755.
